input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: Calling `.strip()` also removes intentional whitespace from the prompt, including the trailing space that separates the prompt from the answer. ANSI removal should preserve that whitespace.
- rationale: When stdout is redirected or otherwise requires ANSI stripping, a normal prompt such as `"Name: "` becomes `"Name:"`. Leading indentation and whitespace-only prompts are also removed, changing the displayed prompt even when it contains no ANSI codes.
critique: The finding identifies the same mechanism as the label. When ANSI stripping is needed, the prompt is also passed through .strip(), which removes the trailing space so 'Name: ' becomes 'Name:' when output is redirected or not a color terminal.
